name: Alain Voge Cornas Les Vieilles Vignes 2013
text:
## Alain Voge Cornas Les Vieilles Vignes 2013

**The story.** Alain Voge, who died aged 81, was one of the leading lights of his generation in [Cornas](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Domaine+Alain+Voge,+Cornas,+France&t=k). His great-grandfather Henri brought the family to the area in the early 20th century, when vines were just one of several crops. Alain started at the estate in 1961 and took the reins with his mother in 1965 after his father's early death. He worked to sell bottled wine, fought to protect the area's vineyards from urban sprawl, and also revived the neighbouring white appellation of [Saint-Péray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-P%C3%A9ray_AOC), where he pioneered barrel fermentation. Decanter's Matt Walls: "To be a leading producer of one appellation is impressive, but to be at the forefront of two is rare indeed." In 2004 Albéric Mazoyer, formerly a winemaking adviser at [Chapoutier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chapoutier), joined as partner and manager, bringing organic and biodynamic certification; Lionel Fraisse succeeded him in 2018 ([Decanter](https://www.decanter.com/obituaries/alain-voge-dies-cornas-rhone-443632/)).

**The wine: Les Vieilles Vignes.** Les Vieilles Vignes was created in the 1970s after replanting in the family vineyards in the heart of Cornas. Its big brother, Les Vieilles Fontaines, from a single site of very old Syrah, is made only in top vintages ([Decanter](https://www.decanter.com/obituaries/alain-voge-dies-cornas-rhone-443632/)). Wine Spectator reports 1,350 cases of the 2013 ([JJ Buckley, critics' notes](https://www.jjbuckley.com/wine/2013-alain-voge-cornas-vieilles-vignes/2013-1298-750)).

**About Cornas.** [Cornas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornas_AOC) is one of the smallest appellations in the Rhône, and makes only red wine, entirely from [Syrah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrah). Its steep east-south-east-facing slopes, between 100 and 400 metres, lie just north of [Valence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valence,_Dr%C3%B4me), south of [Tain-l'Hermitage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tain-l'Hermitage). Sheltered from the cold [mistral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mistral_%28wind%29), it is often the first northern Rhône appellation to begin harvesting ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornas_AOC)).

**From the history books**
- **"Burnt earth."** The name Cornas is said to be Celtic for "burnt earth", and wine is mentioned here as early as 885. [Louis XV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_XV) and [Cardinal Richelieu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Richelieu) are said to have admired it ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornas_AOC)).
- **Bottling at home.** Cornas became an appellation in 1938, but local growers only began bottling their own wine around 1950 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornas_AOC)). Pierre-Auguste Clape, who began estate-bottling in the 1950s, died in 2018 aged 93; Alain Voge, born in 1939, was another of the small group that built Cornas's international reputation ([Decanter](https://www.decanter.com/obituaries/alain-voge-dies-cornas-rhone-443632/)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [northern Rhône vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/northern-rhone) calls 2013 "very promising reds which may well have excellent longevity": despite a slow start and mildew in June, warm days and cool nights through the summer turned the season, and the harvest was one of the latest ever. Albéric Mazoyer told Jeb Dunnuck how hard it was to get ripe tannins, "but there's no tannin issues with this 2013".

**What the critics say for 2013.** As listed by [JJ Buckley](https://www.jjbuckley.com/wine/2013-alain-voge-cornas-vieilles-vignes/2013-1298-750):
- **[Wine Spectator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wine_Spectator): 94** (James Molesworth, November 2015). Old-school Cornas notes of dark bramble, charcoal, olive and bay leaf married to vivid blackberry, raspberry and boysenberry; "everything flows together seamlessly". Best 2017 to 2028.
- **[James Suckling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Suckling): 93** (October 2016). "A complex and fragrant old-vine expression" from a domaine "with a keen eye for purity": dark plum and dark stones, long and deep, with tannins "shaped for the long haul". Best from 2020 and a decade after.
- **[Wine Advocate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wine_Advocate): 92** (Jeb Dunnuck, December 2015). Textbook black cherry, liquid violets, crushed-rock minerality and peppery herbs; medium-bodied depth and integrated acidity. Give it 2 to 3 years, then drink over a decade.
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 91.2** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is thirteen years old. Wine Spectator's window runs to 2028 and Suckling's to about 2030, so it is mature: bramble, olive, charcoal and dark berries. Drink it over the next few years; decant an hour ahead.

**Serving and food.** Serve at 16 to 17°C, with grilled lamb, venison, peppered steak or duck.

**Value and where to buy.** None of the stores on this site lists Alain Voge at the moment; look to fine-wine merchants and auctions.

**Curious details**
- **Two appellations.** Voge is revered in Cornas, but also for reviving Saint-Péray's whites, rare for a single grower ([Decanter](https://www.decanter.com/obituaries/alain-voge-dies-cornas-rhone-443632/)).
